top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single bounded invention: Katori's magic-wavelength condition removes the differential light shift so many neutral atoms can be probed free of Doppler and recoil shifts, and Ye's group demonstrated 10^-18 uncertainty and stability, many-body operation and centimetre-scale gravitational redshift. It has been cross-checked by independent clocks, so maturity is established, and the two-name allocation has no evident missing principal. A narrowly worded citation avoids overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes. The residual costs (ion-clock and ultrastable-laser pioneers, pending redefinition of the second) are smaller than the credit problems in the alternatives, so I prefer an award to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; documented collaborators (L'Huillier, Keller's group, Lund and ETH groups) are not among Katori or Ye, though she works in neighbouring atomic physics
